headline: Highest risk is data leakage from plano’s broad network egress and API calls; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are limited by awesome-python being non-runnable and read-only.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-python is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest plano’s outputs. plano can call APIs and handle config files, but there is no documented shared channel or default bridge. Any injection would require unusual manual copy/paste or external wiring, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies plano output into content sourced from awesome-python, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the two, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Disable manual copy/paste between outputs and prompts during review.
Add provenance labels before any human-mediated transfer.
requires-engineering: add a bridge that strips instruction-like text from shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-python touches no data classes and has no I/O, while plano has broad network egress and sends requests to an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint. If both are pointed at the same workspace or logs, plano can transmit copied content off-box. The pairwise leak is plausible in default deployments once shared artifacts exist.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same workspace or log files, plano can exfiltrate copied contents via its API calls.
IF sensitive material is placed into plano prompts, it can leave the local environment through network egress.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in plano-accessible directories.
Separate workspaces and logs for the two agents.
Review plano prompts before sending them.
Turn off network access for plano in sensitive runs.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on outbound API payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python is non-runnable and has no write surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. plano supports only out-of-process dataplane behavior, has no subprocess spawning, and supports no multiple instances, which limits direct write conflicts. The remaining conflict path is unusual and depends on external shared files not documented here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same config.yaml, file contention can occur.
IF a shared mutable resource is introduced outside the documented profiles, conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Keep shared files read-only for both agents.
Assign separate output directories.
Avoid concurrent edits to config.yaml.
Run plano as a single instance only.
requires-engineering: add file locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-python is a curated collection, so its outputs are likely treated as reference material rather than executable actions. plano, however, is an AI gateway that can route chat completions and may act on upstream text. If plano consumes copied content from awesome-python without verification, errors can cascade into downstream responses or routing decisions.
conditions: IF plano uses content copied from awesome-python as authoritative input, unverified errors can propagate.
IF downstream automation trusts plano outputs without a validation step, the cascade widens.
mitigations: Require human review before plano acts on imported content.
Add a verification step for any facts copied from awesome-python.
Mark reference material as non-authoritative in prompts.
Log source provenance alongside plano outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No sensitive data class, residency constraint, or regulated workload is documented for either agent. awesome-python is a static open-source collection, while plano documents logs/metrics/traces and outbound API use. The only compliance concern visible is ordinary logging hygiene, so the pairwise compliance risk is limited.
conditions: IF regulated data is later routed through plano, retention and residency controls must be re-evaluated.
IF logs contain personal data, the operator must apply the relevant retention policy.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through plano.
Set short log-retention windows.
Review what plano records in logs and metrics.
Document data-handling responsibilities for both agents.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls if regulated data is introduced.
